commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 51 composition encoded its action-incidence flags as equality tests against five specific HTS lines belonging to other chapters, so the branches they gate had no grounding in chapter 51's cited source and were dead for every line in the chapter.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 48. Diff read in full; two hunks only (summary plus the five removed derived rules), no other substantive change.
triage.verifier_justification: The ch51 diff deletes five `derived` rules whose formulas were bare equality tests on HTS statistical reporting numbers belonging to chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95 (`hts_number == "9506.62.40.40"` footballs, `"2203.00.00.30"` beer, `"7202.11.10.00"` ferroalloy, `"7601.10.30.00"` aluminum wire, `"8541.42.00.10"` PV cells), with proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions inside a wool-chapter composition. Those flags gate live components in this module — `china_section_301_component_rate` sums five `if entry_is_line_X and origin_is_china: <list rate>` terms, and `section_122_component_rate` / `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` open with `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0` — so in chapter 51 every one of those branches was permanently false and the §301/§232/§122 incidence layer was identically zero, with no grounding in anything chapter 51's cited source says. The fix removes the ungrounded definitions and re-grounds the identifiers as caller inputs from incidence classification, which is exactly the taxonomy's untraceable_branch (branch removed / re-grounded, formula grounded on the wrong provision). It is not mechanical: whole rules with formulas and proof atoms are deleted and the module's input surface changes, so the summary's retained boilerplate "changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values" is stale and does not describe this diff.
triage.verifier_notes: Re-anchor the citation: the first reader quoted the PR #1300 body, and half of that quote ("gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had") is not in this commit at all — 2a6bdb01de only drops the five derived rules and rewrites the module summary. Better evidence is the module diff itself plus the generator comment added in the same commit (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py): "generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars". Caveats for the corpus: (1) this single generator-level fix rewrites 100 near-identical chapter modules in one commit, so ch51 is one of 100 duplicate instances — dedupe or sample. (2) The repair is partial: in the post file `entry_is_energy_resource` still has formula `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"` and `china_section_301_component_rate`'s proof atoms still cite 7202.11.10.00 / 9506.62.40 / 7601.10.30.00 footnotes inside the chapter-51 module, so the same exemplar coupling survives this commit; the module is made less wrong, not faithful. (3) The fix defers the membership determination to entry preparation rather than encoding it from source, so "re-grounded" here means "ungrounded branch removed", not "correct branch added". (4) Alternative kind considered and rejected: wrong_entity_or_scope (the flags scoped incidence to another chapter's population), but the taxonomy puts "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" and removal-style fixes under untraceable_branch. (5) Note the pre-fix branches were dead-false rather than mis-firing, so the observable wrongness is zero §301/§232/§122 duty for every chapter-51 line; if the corpus wants only mis-firing defects, this is an under-application case.
